title: Carotid and neck artery ultrasound
what: The doctor uses ultrasound to look at the neck arteries that carry blood to the brain. It shows plaques, narrowing, and how blood flows.
why: For dizziness, headaches, ringing in the ears, after a stroke, or with high cholesterol and blood pressure.
duration: usually 20 to 40 minutes; the report is ready right away
tell_doctor: What bothers you: dizziness, weakness in an arm, trouble with speech or vision
High blood pressure, high cholesterol, or diabetes
If you had a stroke or surgery on blood vessels

prepare.title: Prep
prepare.text: Usually none. You can eat and drink.

prepare.title: Neck
prepare.text: Take off necklaces and earrings. No high collars.

prepare.title: Morning
prepare.text: On the day of the test, better to skip extra coffee and smoking. They can affect blood vessels.

steps: You lie on your back with your head turned a little to one side
Gel is put on your neck
The doctor moves the probe along both sides of your neck
Sometimes the vessels behind the ear and above the collarbone are checked
The doctor measures blood flow and wall thickness
feel: Cool gel and light pressure on your neck
You may hear the sound of blood flow. That is normal
after: You can go back to your usual day right away
The report is usually ready right away
If a plaque is found, the doctor will decide on treatment and when to recheck
red_flags: Sudden weakness in an arm or leg, a drooping face, or trouble speaking: call emergency services right away

faq.q: Can the brain's blood vessels be seen?
faq.a: The neck is seen well. Vessels inside the skull are checked with a separate test, transcranial Doppler.
It depends on its size and type. Your doctor will assess it and decide if treatment is needed.

reminders.text: Neck artery ultrasound tomorrow. No prep needed. Take off necklaces and earrings.
